title: Collaborative Development of NLP models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated model debugging and alignment by operationalizing concepts to correct undesired behaviors, specifically focusing on rectifying sentiment and toxicity misclassifications related to Islam (e.g., ensuring 'religion does not connote sentiment' and distinguishing between toxic entities like ISIS and Muslims generally).
findings: Using the CoDev framework in a pilot study, users successfully identified and corrected model bugs related to Islam. For instance, users fixed global model errors that incorrectly predicted negative sentiment for neutral statements like 'Alice practices Islam daily'. They were also able to iteratively clarify concept boundaries to correctly align toxicity labels, distinguishing between violent entities (e.g., 'ISIS is violent' -> non-toxic/factual) and marginalized groups (e.g., 'Muslims are violent' -> toxic).
